lines.t: A rainy dawn, the streets were gray,
I ducked inside to drift away.
The sign above read “Shepherd’s Brew,”
And peace just wrapped me through and through.
The air was rich, a holy scent,
Soft warmth arose where chill was spent.
A kind-eyed man behind the bar
Said, “Welcome, you’ve come so far.”
I glanced above at the shining board,
Names of drinks that praised the Lord:
“Faith Roast Bold,” “Mercy Macchiato,”
“Spirit Steam” and “Grace Gelato.”
“Redeemer’s Roast,” “The Promise Blend,”
“Eternal Light” — it had no end.
He asked me softly, “What’ll it be?”
I said, “Your choice, surprise me.”
Taste and see that the Lord is good,
Stirs my heart the way love would.
Living water fills my soul,
In this cup I’m made whole.
He said, “Whoever drinks of Me
Will never thirst again.”
And I felt my heart begin to mend.
He poured my cup, it shimmered bright,
Like sunrise breaking through the night.
He spoke of peace beyond the rain,
Of love that heals the deepest pain.
“My brew is joy,” He said, “not lore,
It’s grace that flows forevermore.”
Each sip revealed a spark divine,
I knew this drink was more than mine.
Taste and see that the Lord is good,
Stirs my heart the way love would.
Living water fills my soul,
In this cup I’m made whole.
He said, “Whoever drinks of Me
Will never thirst again.”
And I saw heaven shine within.
Then light poured through His quiet grin,
And I knew His face, my sin grew thin.
“Sir,” I gasped, my eyes opened wide,
“You’re Yahushua … right here inside.”
He smiled and said, “My child, it’s true,
I’ve been waiting here for you.”
The mug overflowed, my spirit free,
For Yahushua poured for me.
Now every morning when I wake,
I sip His peace for His sake.
Faith Roast warms my heart anew,
I met my Savior in “Shepherd’s Brew.”
And the sign still whispers like morning dew:
“Taste and see that the Lord is good — it’s true.”
